title: Derived restriction of scalars commutes with $D(f^*)$
statement:
In the situation of [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso], the levelwise functors on the unbounded
derived categories ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) satisfy

$$
D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})\circ D(f^*)\;\cong\;D(f^*)\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})\colon
D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_Y})\longrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}).
$$

proof.text: Work throughout with the categories of module objects in abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale sites, over the pulled-back commutative condensed rings. The small pro-étale sites are essentially small ([sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] lists them as admissible sites), and $\otimes_{\mathbf Z}$ on $\Ab$ is additive in each variable, so [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ gives that each $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ is a Grothendieck abelian category (in particular it has all limits and colimits, so equalizers and coequalizers). By [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] these sheaf tensor products are closed symmetric monoidal and preserve colimits in either variable; tensoring is also additive: preservation of the zero object and binary coproducts preserves their injections and zero maps, hence their projections (characterized by their composites with the injections). It therefore preserves the biproduct diagonal and codiagonal, and the formula $u+v=\nabla\circ(u\oplus v)\circ\Delta$ gives preservation of addition. Thus the hypotheses of clauses 2–4 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] hold. Clause 4 gives exactness of $\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}$ for every coefficient morphism $a$. Restriction is additive: it is the identity on underlying morphisms and the addition of module morphisms is the underlying addition.

source.place: First clause: exactness of restriction of scalars

proof.text: For each of $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda'$, [def-sfb-module-upper-star] defines module pullback as $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$ and states its additivity. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-exact] with coefficient category $\Ab$ to obtain preservation of finite limits and finite colimits by $f^*_{\Ab}$. In particular it preserves the zero object and binary biproducts, so the diagonal/codiagonal calculation in step 1 gives its additivity. Thus it is additive and exact as required by the lifting theorem. The transport in [sk-def-sfb-transport] commutes with the forgetful functors, so [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted], with $F=f^*_{\Ab}$ and $G=\operatorname{mapMod}(f^*_{\Ab})$, gives exactness of this transport. Its ambient module categories satisfy the right-exact tensor hypotheses by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso], $\alpha_f$ is invertible. Since $\alpha_f$ is an isomorphism of monoid objects onto the commutative ring $\Lambda_X$, the monoid $f^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_Y$ is commutative as well (transport the commutativity identity along $\alpha_f$ and naturality of the symmetry), so the hypotheses of clauses 2–3 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] hold for both $\alpha_f$ and $\alpha_f^{-1}$, the ambient category being abelian by step 1. Clauses 4–5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] identify $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_f}$ with the exact functor $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_f^{-1}}$. Consequently module pullback is exact, for both coefficient rings. This uses invertibility of $\alpha_f$, not flatness of $a$.

source.place: First clause: exactness of module pullback for pulled-back coefficients

proof.text: Write $C(F)$ for the functor applying an additive exact functor $F$ termwise to cochain complexes, and $Q_{\mathcal T}:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal T)$ for localization. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], each of the four exact functors above sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and has a levelwise functor $D(F)$ with a natural factorization $D(F)Q_{\mathcal T}\cong Q_{\mathcal T'}C(F)$. These are the levelwise unbounded derived functors of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]; no resolution or boundedness assumption is required.

source.place: First clause: existence of the levelwise derived functors; Stacks Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor)

proof.text: Let $P=\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}\circ f^*_{\Lambda'}$ and $R=f^*_{\Lambda}\circ\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y}$. Write $\eta:P\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ for [def-sfb-comap-upper-star-iso]. For a complex $K$, define the degree-$n$ component of $C(\eta)_K$ to be $\eta_{K^n}$. Naturality of $\eta$ for $d_K^n$ says $R(d_K^n)\eta_{K^n}=\eta_{K^{n+1}}P(d_K^n)$, so these components form a chain map. The inverse chain map has degree-$n$ component $\eta_{K^n}^{-1}$: multiplying the differential equation by the inverse components gives $P(d_K^n)\eta_{K^n}^{-1}=\eta_{K^{n+1}}^{-1}R(d_K^n)$, and the two composites are identities in each degree. For a chain map $h:K\to L$, naturality of $\eta$ gives $R(h^n)\eta_{K^n}=\eta_{L^n}P(h^n)$ in every degree, proving naturality on complexes. This constructs $C(P)\cong C(R)$; applying a composite termwise agrees with composing the termwise functors, on objects, differentials and morphisms.

source.place: Second clause: levelwise extension of the underived natural isomorphism

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal A=\Mod_{\Lambda'_Y}$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. Define $U=D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})\circ D(f^*_{\Lambda'})$ and $V=D(f^*_{\Lambda})\circ D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})$. Applying successively the two factorization isomorphisms from [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives
$$UQ_{\mathcal A}\cong D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})Q_{\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}}C(f^*_{\Lambda'})\cong Q_{\mathcal B}C(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})C(f^*_{\Lambda'})=Q_{\mathcal B}C(P),$$
and, in the same order for the other pair,
$$VQ_{\mathcal A}\cong D(f^*_{\Lambda})Q_{\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}}C(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})\cong Q_{\mathcal B}C(f^*_{\Lambda})C(\operatorname{Res}_{a_Y})=Q_{\mathcal B}C(R).$$
Compose the first isomorphism with $Q_{\mathcal B}C(\eta)$ from step 4 and the inverse of the second. This is a natural isomorphism $UQ_{\mathcal A}\cong VQ_{\mathcal A}$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $Q_{\mathcal A}$, the quasi-isomorphisms, and target $D(\mathcal B)$: the two functors $Q_{\mathcal B}C(P)$ and $Q_{\mathcal B}C(R)$ invert quasi-isomorphisms by step 3, and $U,V$ are their lifts by the displayed factorizations. The resulting natural isomorphism $U\cong V$ is, by construction, the levelwise derived comparison in the statement. Its source is $D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_Y})$ and its target is $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$.

source.place: Second clause: compatibility with composition and descent of the natural isomorphism; Stacks Tags 04VG and 05RU for localization, with natural-transformation lifting as stated in the cited Mathlib leaf

split_report.summary: Verified the current blueprint and underived comparison, expanded exactness for arbitrary commutative condensed coefficient rings, and constructed the comparison explicitly degreewise before descending it through the existing localization universal-property node. Removed the earlier attempt’s redundant new derived-functor lemma: existing Mathlib-leaf nodes already supply factorization and lifting. No statement change, no new nodes, no Lean work. Second reading made tensor and inverse-image additivity explicit, and wrote the inverse chain-map and chain-map naturality equations.
blueprint: Unit sk-def-sfb-coefficient-comparisons, step 2, final clause: restriction commutes with pullback levelwise on derived categories. Steps 1–3 realize the first clause of the item proof (exactness and levelwise extension); steps 4–5 realize its second clause (compatibility with natural isomorphisms and composition).

tool_uses.why: Exactness of inverse image with coefficient category Ab, needed for module transport; the coefficient-comparison unit supplies no inverse-image exactness theorem.
Generic lifting of exactness from underlying abelian sheaves to module objects; it verifies a hypothesis of the levelwise construction rather than replacing any unit step.
Invertibility of the cartesian coefficient morphism, explicitly invoked by step 2 of the comparison unit; this holds for every condensed ring.

Generic structure theorem for sheaves on an essentially small site: Sh(X_proét, Ab) is Grothendieck abelian with additive closed tensor, the abelian/limit hypotheses of change-of-scalars clauses 3-4 and of the lifted-exactness lemma; no node of the route states abelianness of these sheaf categories (same accepted tool as in lem-sfb-module-upper-star-kflat-quasi-iso).
